ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The Michaelis equation is expressed in the form $y=\frac{V_\mathrm{max}[S]}{K_\mathrm{m}+[S]}$, where $y$ represents the reaction rate, $[S]$ represents the substrate concentration, $V_\mathrm{max}$ represents the maximum reaction rate, and $K_\mathrm{m}$ represents the Michaelis constant. When a competitive inhibitor is added to the reaction system, the value of $a$ in the expression (that is, $\frac{V_\mathrm{max}}{K_\mathrm{m}}$) will decrease.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image gives the Lineweaver-Burk double-reciprocal equation: 1/V = (Km/Vmax)·1/[S] + 1/Vmax. Therefore, in the double-reciprocal straight line, the coefficient multiplying 1/[S] is Km/Vmax, which is the slope of the straight line. The context of the problem is adding a competitive inhibitor. The rule of competitive inhibition is that Vmax remains unchanged, while the apparent Km increases. Because Km increases and Vmax remains unchanged, Km/Vmax increases. Therefore, the change in the value of a corresponding to the double-reciprocal equation in the figure should be an increase.
